steps: Midpoint triangle DEF has sides half of BC, CA, AB
∆BDE, ∆ADF, ∆ECF each have the same half-length sides, so congruent to ∆DEF
∆ABC has sides twice as long, so not congruent
check_code:
from fractions import Fraction as F
A=(F(0),F(0));B=(F(7),F(0));C=(F(2),F(5))
mid=lambda P,Q:((P[0]+Q[0])/2,(P[1]+Q[1])/2)
D=mid(A,B);E=mid(B,C);Fp=mid(A,C)
d2=lambda P,Q:(P[0]-Q[0])**2+(P[1]-Q[1])**2
sides=lambda P,Q,R:sorted([d2(P,Q),d2(Q,R),d2(R,P)])
ref=sides(D,E,Fp)
opts={'A':sides(B,D,E),'B':sides(A,D,Fp),'C':sides(E,C,Fp),'D':sides(A,B,C)}
notcong=[k for k,v in opts.items() if v!=ref]
assert notcong==['D']

k=180/6
d=3*k-1*k
opts={'A':15,'B':30,'C':45,'D':60}
assert d==opts['D']
for o in 'ABC': assert d!=opts[o]

method: Coincident line system has infinitely many common solutions
steps: Every point on the line is common, so infinitely many intersections
check_code:
import sympy as sp
x,y=sp.symbols('x y')
sol=sp.solve([2*x+3*y-6, 4*x+6*y-12],[x,y],dict=True)
# one free parameter -> infinitely many solutions
assert len(sol)==1 and len(sol[0])==1
kind='infinite'
opts={'A':'infinite','B':'unique','C':'finite','D':'none'}
assert kind==opts['A']
for o in 'BCD': assert kind!=opts[o]

import sympy as sp
a,b=sp.symbols('a b')
s=sp.solve([sp.Eq(b-1,2*(a-1)),sp.Eq(3*(b+9),4*(a+9))],[a,b])
t=s[a]+s[b]
opts={'A':17,'B':15,'C':21,'D':30}
assert t==opts['A']
for o in 'BCD': assert t!=opts[o]

import sympy as sp

import sympy as sp
t=sp.symbols('t')
e=(1+sp.sin(t)-sp.cos(t))/(1+sp.sin(t)+sp.cos(t))
opts={'A':sp.tan(t/2),'B':sp.cos(t/2),'C':sp.cot(t/2),'D':sp.sin(t/2)}
vals=[sp.Rational(3,10),sp.Rational(7,10),sp.Rational(11,10)]
ok=lambda f: all(abs(sp.N((e-f).subs(t,v)))<1e-12 for v in vals)
assert ok(opts['A'])
for o in 'BCD': assert not ok(opts[o])
